newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MANCINI AND ERIKSSON SIGN FOR LAZIO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCINI AND ERIKSSON SIGN FOR LAZIO.

text.p: Striker Roberto Mancini signed a preliminary contract with Italian club Lazio on Monday while German captain Juergen Klinsmann arrived in Genoa to be presented as his Sampdoria replacement.

Lazio said Mancini, who technically remains contracted to Sampdoria until the end of June, had signed a preliminary three-year contract in Rome after meeting president Dino Zoff and majority shareholder Sergio Cragnotti.

Mancini, 32, who has spent the last 15 seasons with Sampdoria, was joined by Sampdoria's Swedish coach Sven-Goran Eriksson, his deputy Luciano Spinosi, masseur Paolo Vigano and trainer Carlo Focardi in a mass move.
Club sources said Eriksson's deal was worth around $900,000 a season, Mancini's a total of $1.8 million.
Sampdoria had already announced that Mancini, one of the greatest players in the history of Sampdoria and a crowd hero, would be replaced by Klinsmann.
The former Bayern Munich striker, speaking fluent Italian, said Sampdoria had offered less than other clubs.
But "I was looking for a serious and ambitious club that could give me the chance to show Italians that I have improved in the last few years," he said.
"I found all this at Samp and with president (Enrico) Mantovani we decided to sign an annual contract but we have also discussed the possibility of extending it."
Klinsmann said that nobody could replace Mancini "who was and remains the standard-bearer for Sampdoria.
"And on a technical level we are different players. For my part, I will try and do my utmost to please the fans."
Klinsmann will wear the number 18 shirt. Sampdoria has said it is considering withdrawing the number 10 shirt worn by Mancini as a mark of respect for the departed great.
The German played in Italy previously at the end of the 1980s with Internazionale and has a holiday home on Lake Como north of Milan.
He said he still had great memories of Inter, especially his first two years at the club.
Klinsmann said that his arguments with Trapattoni, his coach at Inter and Bayern, were mostly over tactics.
"I am a striker and like attacking football. For him the result comes first of all."
